articles.title: Why Alberto Mendoza transferred from Indiana to Georgia Tech out of brother's shadow
articles.summary: Fernando Mendoza's brother is getting his first chance to be a starting quarterback at the collegiate level.
articles.body:
As Fernando Mendoza waits his turn in the NFL, his little brother's turn to start has finally arrived.

Alberto Mendoza will open the season as Georgia Tech's starting quarterback after transferring from Indiana, where he backed up his brother during a dream season for both the Mendoza family and the Hoosiers.

A day after the national championship game, the younger Mendoza decided to head to the ACC and replace Haynes King as the Yellow Jackets' quarterback.

Here's what you need to know about Mendoza's move to Georgia Tech.

Why did Alberto Mendoza transfer from Indiana to Georgia Tech?

All that could have made Indiana's story better was Alberto Mendoza succeeding his brother as the Hoosiers' starting quarterback after a national championship season. That wasn't in the cards, though.

By the time the younger Mendoza entered the transfer portal on Jan. 20, Indiana had already landed its starter for 2026: TCU's Josh Hoover.

Why wouldn't Curt Cignetti just keep it in the family and promise the job to Alberto Mendoza? That would have been a major gamble for a program with title hopes. Mendoza doesn't have any starting experience at the collegiate level, and he was a three-star recruit who ranked 137th in his class.

Cignetti's first two quarterbacks at Indiana both had multiple years of starting experience, between Kurtis Rourke's time at Ohio and Fernando Mendoza's time at California. That strategy worked quite well. By adding Hoover rather than passing the baton to Mendoza, Cignetti stuck to his guns and freed up Mendoza to find a starting opportunity elsewhere.

At Georgia Tech, Mendoza beat out redshirt freshman Grady Adamson and will replace Haynes King, who finished 10th in Heisman Trophy voting last season.

Mendoza ranked 137th out of all quarterbacks in the 2024 recruiting class, according to 247 Sports, coming in at three stars. He committed to Indiana a year before his brother joined him in Bloomington, which means the Hoosiers' dream season might have never happened had the program not given the younger Mendoza brother an offer.

To Alberto's credit, Fernando wasn't a highly-ranked recruit, either. Fernando was similarly a three-star quarterback who ranked 134th at his position. Alberto has already punched above his weight by becoming a Power Four starter, and he now has a chance to prove he should have been his brother's successor at Indiana.

Mendoza was relegated to mop-up duty at Indiana last season, tossing only 24 passes for the Hoosiers with his brother starting every game.

While his time on the field was limited, he impressed. Mendoza threw five touchdown passes on 24 attempts, giving Georgia Tech fans something to be excited about as he becomes a starter for the first time at this level.

articles.body:
The San Francisco 49ers are going on a field trip to start the year! The Niners will be one of the two teams who will play the first-ever NFL game in Australia when they take on the Los Angeles Rams. For many players, it's an awesome opportunity to visit a different country. However, it seems like star DE Nick Bosa didn't sound too thrilled about the prospect of playing in Australia.

Bosa was asked by a few reporters about what he's most excited about to see in Australia. The 49ers star seemed unenthusiastic, sighing before admitting that he doesn't know a lot about the country. He did say that he heard that Australia has good coffee, so he's excited to try that out.

Both Bosa and George Kittle will be travelling to Australia with the 49ers for their Week 1 game against the Rams. That being said, they still aren't exactly locks to play in Week 1 of the season. Of the two, Kittle is more likely to suit up against Los Angeles . Bosa, on the other hand, is still recovering from his injury, but he's expressed optimism that he'll suit up for his team to start the season.

Bosa suffered a torn ACL just three weeks into the 2025 season. This was an unfortunate development for the 49ers star, who was coming off one of his best seasons in recent memory. In his last healthy season in 2024, Bosa played 14 games and recorded nine sacks, 30 tackles, a forced fumble, a pass deflection, and an interception. Bosa already had two sacks and two forced fumbles in his three games before being ruled out.

Even if Bosa doesn't end up playing or is put on a snap count for Week 1, the 49ers are confident in their ability to get production from their other pass-rushers. Defensive coordinator Raheem Morris had this to say earlier this week.

"I feel pretty deep there," Morris said when asked about the 49ers' depth. "Obviously, we had a bunch of guys, got a couple of guys claimed. Well, one guy claimed in particular, but we have some young guys we brought in here this year… You got a bunch of different people in it that can play, give you some good rotational pieces to do some good things."

articles.body:
The FIA has issued a Heat Hazard for this weekend's Italian Grand Prix , with temperatures to exceed 31 degrees.

The guideline, which was introduced for the 2025 season, allows teams to fit advanced driver cooling systems during the race weekend.

The systems are not mandatory, however, and if drivers opt against them, their cars will be fitted with ballast to offset the 5kg weight of the devices.

A statement from FIA Formula 1 Race Director Rui Marques read: "In accordance with Article B1.5.10 of the FIA F1 Regulations, having received a forecast from the Official Weather Service predicting that the Heat Index will be greater than 31.0 °C at some time during the Race at this Competition, a Heat Hazard is declared."

Friday sessions are expected to take place at 33 degrees, rising to 34 degrees for Saturday and Sunday.

The first Heat Hazard was issued at the swealtering 2025 Singapore Grand Prix and again at the 2026 Austrian Grand Prix.

Regarding the cooling devices, Article 26.19 of the FIA F1 Sporting Regulations reads: "Any driver may elect not to wear any items of personal equipment that form part of the Driver Cooling System. In such circumstances, all other components, including any cooling medium, of the Driver Cooling System must be fitted.

"In addition, the difference in mass between the driver's personal equipment normally used and any items of a driver's personal equipment that form part of the system must be compensated by the fitting of 0.5kg of ballast in the cockpit."

Mercedes' George Russell, who is the director of the Grand Prix Drivers' Association, explained the cooling device in further detail

"We've used the driver cooling vest already a few times at the hot races but this is the first time it's been mandatory," he commented.

"I think it's good news. Not everybody finds the top comfortable but over time you'll be able to adjust it to your own preferences.

"The concept is good and when you're racing in 90 per cent humidity and the cockpits at 60 degrees it becomes a sauna inside the car so we all welcome it."

articles.title: 4 things to watch for ahead of Fiorentina vs Torino
articles.summary: The Viola have plenty to work on ahead of their first game after the window closes.
articles.body:
You'd be hard-pressed to find a more balanced matchup in Serie A than Torino vs. Fiorentina. Each of the last three matches between the two sides have ended in a stalemate, and you'd have to go back all the way to January 10, 2022 for the last time the two were separated by more than one goal.

Fiorentina kicked off their season with a 4-1 win vs. Benevento in the Coppa Italia before losing 4-0 and 3-0 to Roma and Frosinone. Torino, meanwhile, edged Carrarese 1-0 in the cup before losing 2-1 to Milan and Sassuolo, followed by a 1-0 defeat to Monza in the cup. Both teams are struggling to adjust to life under their new managers, and both are in desperate need of a win. So, which team will come out on top? Let's take a look at the four main things to keep an eye on for this one.

1. Fiorentina's rest-defense when the fullbacks push up

In their first two matches under Fabio Grosso, Fiorentina have shown a willingness to get their fullbacks involved, but their opponents have exposed how vulnerable they can be when possession is lost. We saw this in their first match vs. Roma, when they were sliced open with a basic long ball out from the back. Their defenders were caught off guard and enabled Paulo Dybala and Donyell Malen to combine for the second goal. And we saw this vs. Frosinone, with the defenders getting caught ball-watching and enabling Antonio Raimondo to pick up the ball unmarked and smash home a trivela volley.

Fiorentina aren't going to change their ways just to get past Torino, but they do need to answer some uncomfortable questions about their tactical balance. Who stays underneath the ball when Fiorentina attack? Does Arthur Atta drop between/alongside the CBs? Does one fullback stay while the other advances? How quickly can Torino attack the space behind the advanced fullback? If Torino can consistently get their wingback + inside forward attacking the same channel, then Fiorentina could be in for a long night.

He wasn't able to showcase his talent at Real Madrid, but Franco Mastantuono has already looked like Fiorentina's most dangerous individual attacking player. After a promising display that saw him win 4 fouls and make 4 progressive carries vs. Roma, Mastantuono fared even better against Frosinone. He repeatedly received on the right, attacked defenders and combined nicely with the players around him, making 2 key passes, 5 progressive carries, and 7 shots. It's no surprise that the top US betting sites for soccer have tipped him for a prominent role vs. Torino.

The biggest question is whether Torino can force him inside into traffic or whether he gets isolated against left back Alessio Cacciamani. Does he stay wide, receive facing forward and attack 1v1? Or does he come inside early, receive between the lines, and allow the fullback to overlap? If Torino's defenders get pinned deep, Fiorentina could potentially create a pretty favorable 2v1 and dominate the flow of the match. With 12 goals from their first three matches, Fiorentina know this one could be high-scoring, and it's vital that they force the issue and use Mastantuono's technical craft to their advantage.

When Fiorentina take the field at the Stadio Artemio Franchi, it won't be Moise Kean leading the line, but Beto. The interesting question isn't just whether Beto scores, but what type of reference point he gives the attack. We've seen throughout his meteoric ascent from Portimonense to Udinese to Everton that he has what it takes to do multiple things at once, be that pinning the center backs deep, or threatening with his incisive runs, or attacking crosses/cutbacks and connecting with his attacking partners.

If Beto occupies the central defenders effectively, that should create much more room for the wide players, and he should also be able to provide far more of a reference point up top, thus enabling Fiorentina to avoid playing out from the back with risky, short passes. By serving as a target man to pin back the defenders and allowing Fiorentina to go Route One with their attacking, Beto could very well end up being an upgrade over Kean.

4. Torino's ability to attack the space around Fiorentina's CBs

It's a battle of the ex-Premier League strikers as Beto goes up against Che Adams, who is expected to retain his starting place ahead of the likes of Duvan Zapata and Giovanni Simeone. The important thing isn't necessarily Adams' finishing. It's whether he can: occupy the center backs pull one out, create a channel for the attacking midfielders like Gvidas Gineitis to attack, and threaten behind if Fiorentina push their line higher. Fiorentina's defensive organization has been their biggest weakness so far, so Torino don't need 20 chances; they just need to repeatedly create the same advantageous situation and test their mettle.

Fiorentina have already had quite a few issues defending set pieces, and their defensive organization has been erratic at best. Against a team playing with three center backs and plenty of size, Torino could very well exploit Fiorentina's backline both from open play as well as dead-ball scenarios. Fiorentina fans will be hoping that their new signings like Beto and Pedro Goncalves can hit the ground running as they seek to ascend off the bottom of the Serie A table.

articles.title: AJ Blubaugh has become Houston Astros' do-everything bullpen weapon. 'What he's doing is incredible'
articles.summary: AJ Blubaugh has pitched in every inning this season. Now the Astros are trusting their rookie reliever with some of their biggest outs.
articles.body:
Veiled somewhat by his role and veteran colleagues is the value AJ Blubaugh has brought to the Houston Astros ' bullpen in his rookie season. Other relievers eclipse him in wins above replacement, but none can rival the variety of the right-hander's contributions.

Blubaugh, a converted starter , has helped buoy and preserve Houston 's pitching staff by being an option at any time. He has entered at least one game this season in every inning from one through nine. He has worked multiple innings in 33 of 53 appearances.

No major-league reliever has thrown more innings than Blubaugh, who has a 3.06 ERA in 85 ⅓ frames. That combination alone illustrates Blubaugh's importance to an Astros bullpen that entered Wednesday with the sport's fifth-lowest ERA since May 1.

At a critical point in the season, however, his position in it also appears to be evolving. In Blubaugh's first 41 outings, he recorded four holds, defined as a reliever entering a save situation and maintaining a lead for the next reliever while getting at least one out.

In his 11 outings in August, Blubaugh recorded four holds. That included both his appearances during the Astros' week in New York against the Yankees and Mets . He also logged a save last month and, in his first outing of September, entered a scoreless game in the eighth inning Wednesday against the White Sox .

"The moments are not getting too big for him anymore," manager Joe Espada said after his team's 2-0 win Wednesday night . "Obviously, I'm starting to give him the ball in big spots, because he's earned the right to do that. He can pitch out of trouble, he can get punchouts."

Since allowing five runs at Coors Field in his fifth outing of the season, Blubaugh has a 2.22 ERA over his past 48 appearances. He has allowed one earned run in his past 18 innings while drawing higher-leverage situations for a Houston team in a postseason hunt.

The implications for its bullpen are enticing. Closer Josh Hader has been excellent since his return in June from the injured list, going 22-for-22 in save chances with a 0.72 ERA. Bryan Abreu has turned his season around to reassume a setup role alongside Steven Okert .

Adding Blubaugh to the late-innings mix could expand Espada's options to close out games with a well-worked bullpen. Some caveats do exist. Blubaugh is still relatively new to that at the major-league level, and his multi-inning ability can be needed earlier in games. His workload also bears watching.

Blubaugh ended Wednesday with 10 ⅓ innings more than any other reliever in the majors this season. His 33 multi-inning appearances also lead the majors. He does not operate by finesse, either; his fastball has averaged 95.7 mph this season and touched 99.3 mph.

"What's funny, if no one told me I had a high workload, I wouldn't know I had a high workload," Blubaugh said Wednesday night. "I'm approaching every day as I'm trying to pitch, and whether I feel good or I feel bad doesn't change anything.

"Whether I go in in the first inning or the eighth inning tonight, I'm still trying to put up a zero. So I wouldn't say I feel any certain way. Tomorrow I'm going to show up the same way, I'm going to do my prep and I'm going to make myself available to throw."

After throwing two scoreless innings at Citi Field on Sunday, Blubaugh did not pitch the next two days. Wednesday, the Astros reached the eighth inning of a scoreless tie with the AL Central-leading White Sox, whose lineup featured seven left-handed or switch-hitters.

None of their relievers save Kai-Wei Teng and Tatsuya Imai had pitched Tuesday . Okert and Abreu had each worked Sunday and Monday, however. Left-hander Bennett Sousa has struggled to get lefties out this year. Blubaugh came in holding lefties to a .550 OPS. He drew the eighth.

Tristan Peters met him with a leadoff triple, driving a fastball off the base of the wall in right-center at Daikin Park. Blubaugh walked Drew Romo , the Chicago ninth hitter, turning their lineup over. After the walk, he said, he resolved "to start pounding the zone and pray for good things to happen."

One did. With the Astros infield in, Sam Antonacci bounced a first-pitch sweeper to shortstop Jeremy Peña . Peters hesitated before breaking for home plate. Peña threw him out.

"I thought the big play was that ground ball to Jeremy, Peters tried to kind of deke him and hesitated to go, potentially thinking (he'd) go for a double play," Espada said. "So he was waiting to see what Jeremy was going to do, but Jeremy held his ground, made the right decision there."

Blubaugh agreed "you could feel (the inning) switch there." But it wasn't over. Munetaka Murakami hit a 2-2 sweeper to right-center. Romo, the catcher running at second base, was held at third. Miguel Vargas arrived with the bases loaded and one out. Blubaugh threw him two fastballs.

"Throw it as hard as I can, that's really what it came down to," Blubaugh said. "Empty the tank, give everything I have right here, get this out and then go from there. And it just happened to get in there and jam him a little bit."

A 97 mph fastball on the plate induced a sharp grounder to third baseman Isaac Paredes , who started a double play. Nelson Velázquez's two-out, bases-loaded single in the bottom of the inning gave Houston the lead. Hader preserved it, as the Astros stretched their AL West lead back to two games.

Espada credited Blubaugh with "staying composed, pitching and getting the job done." The situation may have magnified it. But the result resembled much of Blubaugh's season before it.

"What he's doing is incredible," said starter Hayden Wesneski , who allowed one hit over seven scoreless innings Wednesday. "It's so hard. I've been in that role and I didn't do that. He fills a role of, like, whatever you need. And what he's doing is incredible."

articles.title: Journalist believes Liverpool made huge £30m transfer mistake
articles.summary: David Lynch Says Liverpool Made £30m Transfer Mistake With MamardashviliLiverpool’s recruitment strategy has produced some enormous deals, but David Lynch be...
articles.body:
David Lynch Says Liverpool Made £30m Transfer Mistake With Mamardashvili

Liverpool's recruitment strategy has produced some enormous deals, but David Lynch believes one previous decision now stands out as a significant mistake.

Speaking to Dave Davis on Anfield Index's Media Matters podcast, Lynch questioned Liverpool's move for Giorgi Mamardashvili and suggested the subsequent signing of highly rated young goalkeeper Lucca Brughmans represents a change of direction.

For Lynch, the problem centres on one fundamental requirement. Liverpool need a goalkeeper comfortable with the ball at his feet, and Mamardashvili has struggled to provide it.

Mamardashvili Transfer Questioned By Lynch

Liverpool originally agreed a deal worth around £30 million for Mamardashvili before the Georgian goalkeeper eventually arrived at Anfield.

Lynch believes his profile has proven unsuitable for the way Liverpool want to play.

"We've spoken about it with Mamardashvili," Lynch told Davis. "It just looks so far from the level in terms of with the ball at his feet."

That issue becomes particularly important because Liverpool continue to involve their goalkeeper heavily in possession.

"They clearly haven't done that. They need the goalkeeper to be good with the feet. And on that basis, Mamardashvili was a bizarre signing."

Brughmans Deal Signals Different Direction

Liverpool's move for Brughmans provided the backdrop to Lynch's assessment.

The teenager was attracting significant interest before Liverpool secured him, and Lynch highlighted one particular quality.

"You look at kind of the numbers behind him and he looks a decent shot stopper early on," he said. "He looks really good with his feet."

That difference between the two goalkeepers is why Lynch believes Liverpool's latest transfer could represent an acknowledgement of their previous mistake.

"This to me looks like a correction of that."

He added: "If you were to criticise any element of the transfer approach in recent years, I think Mamardashvili goes up there as kind of one of the big mistakes they've made."

Mamardashvili's reputation was built significantly upon his ability to stop shots, something Lynch readily acknowledged.

"An unbelievable shot stopper at Valencia, but just not good enough with his feet."

The difficulty, according to Lynch, is improving that aspect sufficiently for Liverpool's requirements.

"You've never seen a keeper either who's bad with his feet who's then learned to be good with his feet. That's one of those innate skills, isn't it? You either have it or you don't and he never did really."

There could still be an important financial consideration if Liverpool eventually decide to move Mamardashvili on.

"Now, of course, they probably can get the money back on him, which is good," Lynch said.

£30m Decision Leaves Liverpool With Questions

Liverpool's decision to recruit another goalkeeper therefore carries significance beyond the arrival of an exciting young prospect.

Brughmans represents a markedly different profile, particularly in possession. Lynch believes that tells its own story about how Liverpool now view the position.

"What an odd signing that was and one that didn't ever seem like he was going to be a fit."

Liverpool have shown a willingness to plan years ahead when recruiting players, particularly goalkeepers. On this occasion, Lynch believes the original succession plan has failed to develop as intended.

Brughmans now offers another possible route forward.

As Lynch concluded: "I think this is a good signing. He seems a smart signing."

For Liverpool, finding the right successor to Alisson remains an enormous decision. Their latest move suggests the search for that answer continues.

articles.summary: The winner of the 70th edition of the Ballon d'Or will be selected this October, as the best player from the 2025/26 season will be identified and bestowed w...
articles.body:
The winner of the 70th edition of the Ballon d'Or will be selected this October, as the best player from the 2025/26 season will be identified and bestowed with the most prestigious individual award the sport of soccer has to offer.

Last year's winner, Rodri, could be in the running for another award, after he helped lead Spain to a World Cup title this past summer.

This year's edition is special, held at a different location from usual to celebrate the anniversary milestone.

The Sporting News brings you a look at when the shortlist of nominees will be released, as the best players in the world will learn if they are up for the famous trophy this time around.

When are the Ballon d'Or nominees announced?

France Football will officially announce the nominees for men's and women's 2026 Ballon d'Or on Tuesday, September 8 between 11 a.m. and 4 p.m. CET .

A 30-player shortlist will be revealed, from which the winner will eventually be selected.

At the gala, the votes will be tallied and the 30 players will be ranked from bottom to top, with the top-ranked player winning the award.

The 2026 Ballon d'Or will be awarded at a ceremony on Monday, October 26 .

While the ceremony is usually held in Paris, France, the gala for the 70th edition of the men's trophy will be held this time in London, England. This is to honor inaugural winner, Sir Stanley Matthews.

A panel of international journalists compiled by France Football comes up with the 30 finalists for the men's Ballon d'Or and the Yashin Award shortlist for the world's best goalkeeper.

Also, a group of 50 international women's soccer journalists picks the women's Ballon d'Or. Lastly, a panel of 32 former Ballon d'Or winners nominates the 10 Kopa Trophy finalists (under-21 players).

The reduction in the number of jurors is anticipated to bring more objectivity, with a focus on individual excellence and who is most deserving of being the overall winner of the Ballon d'Or.

Madrid's voluble protests over Rodri's win and Messi's disputed triumph in 2023 see the new system already under strain.

Deion Sanders begins Year 4 at Colorado in the city where he became a legend, as the Buffaloes face Georgia Tech in Atlanta on Thursday.

Sanders played for the Falcons and Braves in the early 1990s, a rare two-sport star in the pros, and remains an iconic figure in Atlanta sports history. Though his legacy could earn him a warm welcome at Bobby Dodd Stadium, that nostalgia won't do much for the Buffs as they try to bounce back from a 3-9 season.

Second-year quarterback Julian Lewis, who starred down the road at Carrollton High School, will lead a Colorado offense that loaded up with transfers in the offseason. That includes receivers Kam Perry (Miami Ohio), DeAndre Moore Jr. (Texas) and Danny Scudero (San Jose State), who are among 43 transfers on the roster.

Speaking of transfers, the Yellow Jackets will roll out a high-profile pair in QB Alberto Mendoza, late of Indiana and brother of the 2025 Heisman Trophy winner, and former Michigan and Alabama running back Justice Haynes, who grew up in suburban Atlanta. Whatever happens there, things figure to look quite a bit different for Tech after Haynes King held down the QB position the last three years.

articles.title: Colorado football predictions 2026: Projecting Deion Sanders' make-or-break season in Year 3
articles.summary: Deion Sanders enters 2026 with a 16-21 overall record at Colorado.
articles.body:
For Deion Sanders and the Colorado Buffaloes , 2026 is a crucial year. Although Sanders arrived in Boulder with a 19-2 record across three seasons at Jackson State, his tenure at Colorado has gone poorly.

Through three seasons, he has a 16-21 record, including a 3-9 finish last year and a 1-8 record in the Big 12. He went 4-8 in his first season in 2023. His lone successful year was a 9-4 finish in 2024, when Shedeur Sanders and Travis Hunter both had career-best seasons.

As Sanders enters his fourth season, he will be coaching to keep his job at Colorado in 2026. Let's take a look at each game on the Buffs' schedule to try to predict just how this season will go for Sanders and company.

PRESEASON RANKINGS: All 138 teams | All 138 coaches

How this one goes will likely help define the entire season for Colorado, and we're in for a treat on the first big Thursday night college football game of the season. Colorado won this one last year, 27-20, at home, but now has to face the Yellow Jackets on the road.

Brent Key has made Tech into a consistent winner in Atlanta, but this year he has to break in a new quarterback in Alberto Mendoza. Yes, there's another Mendoza in college football, the younger brother of Indiana and new Las Vegas Raiders franchise quarterback Fernando. Unlike his older brother, Alberto will be playing for Georgia Tech.

Colorado returns quarterback Julian Lewis as well as leading rusher Micah Welch from last season, but the defense is entirely new. I like Mendoza and returning running back Malachi Hosley to win at home, but Colorado keeps it competitive.

Weber State got off to a 1-0 start this season, winning on the road to Northern Colorado thanks to a missed extra point by the Bears that would have forced overtime.

The Wildcats have gone 4-8 the last two seasons, and Colorado will get a bounce back win against lesser competition at home in this one. If this goes the other way though, Sanders could potentially be on the chopping block in a matter of days.

Colorado historically doesn't do well against Big Ten opponents, with a 3-8 record in the last 11 meetings. Two years ago, the Buffs went on the road and lost to a mediocre Nebraska team 28-10. The Wildcats have Chip Kelly at offensive coordinator, and bring in Michigan State transfer quarterback Aiden Chiles. Northwestern also brings back running back Caleb Komolafe.

Colorado's defense lost virtually everyone from the unit last year, but brings in a ton of portal players like FCS star Lamont Lester Jr. and Tulane's Santana Hopper. Sanders also hired former Virginia Tech defensive coordinator Chris Marve, so the unit should improve. I like the Wildcats at home in this one.

Noticing a trend here? Colorado has a tough travel schedule in September, playing three of its first four games on the road. The Buffs have to go on the road to face a Baylor team that's re-energized with DJ Lagway under center.

After a tough break at Florida, he's expected to drastically improve as he plays in Texas again, where he broke high school records. Baylor head coach Dave Aranda has lost his last three Big 12 openers, but take the Bears at home.

Colorado gets a much-needed return to its home stadium this week. Unfortunately for the Buffs, the defending Big 12 champions come to town in what is Homecoming for Colorado.

Colorado has the horses to play well against the Red Raiders, as the Buffs won 41-27 the last time these two played in 2024. But I think Texas Tech is just too talented, and takes over late in the game to spoil Colorado's Homecoming this year.

Colorado rebounds and gets a much-needed win here. Yes, the Buffs lost 53-7 last year, but the Utes will take a slight step back without Kyle Whittingham at the helm. The Buffs get this one coming off of a bye, whereas Utah plays Kansas the week before.

This one might be ugly. Oklahoma State has hired Eric Morris from North Texas, and he brought virtually his entire team with him, including star quarterback Drew Mestemaker. North Texas finished first overall last season in scoring offense, averaging 45 points per game, and OSU is expected to light up opposing defenses this season.

Kansas State has Collin Klein as its head coach, as the former Wildcat quarterback looks to continue a winning tradition in Manhattan. Colorado is 0-2 against K-State in the last two meetings, but both the last time these two played in Boulder, Sanders' team lost by a field goal. Give me the Buffs in a close one here at home.

Just one season after making a dream College Football Playoff appearance, the Sun Devils took a step back last year, finishing 8-5. Arizona State won this one 42-17 last season, and going on the road to play in Tempe is a tough task. Colorado can keep this one close for most of it, though.

Houston is expected to have a breakthrough season as Willie Fritz enters his fourth season. But Colorado gets this one at home, and it'll be a Friday night game on Fox which should enhance the atmosphere. Colorado wins a much-needed close one here.

Colorado stays hot here and continues to play well, getting the Bearcats with an extra day of rest from playing on Friday. Cincinnati has lost its last four Senior Day games at home, falling to Tulane, Kansas, TCU and BYU at home. The Buffs win a close one to enter the final week of the regular season fighting for bowl eligibility.

In UCF's first season running it back with Scott Frost, the Knights finished 5-7. Unfortunately the Knights play in sunny Orlando, Fla., it is likely going to be quite cold in Boulder for this one in late November.

As someone who grew up in Orlando, I can confidently say firsthand we are not built for this. Colorado closes out the season on a high note, giving Sanders a victory to send the Buffs to bowl season.

articles.title: Red Bull’s third ADUO assessment could come too late for 2026 title challenge
articles.summary: Red Bull could be locked in a race against the clock as a massive F1 engine crisis looms that could dominate early discussions at the Italian GP in Monza. As...
articles.body:
Red Bull could be locked in a race against the clock as a massive F1 engine crisis looms that could dominate early discussions at the Italian GP in Monza.

As the technical landscape of the new regulations continues to evolve, the ongoing ADUO debate is emerging as a critical focal point for the sport's leading power unit manufacturers.

At the sharp end of this discussion is Red Bull Powertrains, where the approaching third assessment window presents a high-stakes operational dilemma dictated entirely by manufacturing realities.

Internal combustion and hybrid powertrain programmes require immense lead times. Component design, dynamometer validation, casting, and precision machining collectively demand lead times in the region of 36 weeks.

Consequently, by the time the FIA conducts its third scheduled evaluation window, Red Bull may find itself boxed into a corner by its own production calendar.

Should the data from this forthcoming assessment allow for engine improvements, the actual scope for practical development will be severely restricted, something which critics have questioned .

Simultaneously, an intriguing counterpoint is developing as Mercedes, who have been permitted engine developments under the second ADUO assessment, much to Red Bull's confusion.

Ultimately, the divergent situations facing Red Bull and Mercedes illustrate the intricate operational tightrope of contemporary Formula 1.

While Red Bull grapples with the unyielding problem of restrictions and potential component lead times, Mercedes faces the strategic challenge of capitalising on unspent capacity.

And that all does not bode well for Max Verstappen to launch a late surge for the F1 championship, for any ADUO benefits Red Bull do receive on the third review could come too late.

Mercedes has dominated the early 2026 races in Melbourne, Shanghai and Suzuka, underscoring its power unit as the current benchmark after the regulation overhaul.

The FIA's new ADUO system aims to narrow that gap by granting underperforming manufacturers extra dyno time and additional upgrades based on how far they trail the reference.

With Bahrain and Saudi Arabia canceled, the first six-race engine evaluation may be brought forward, a move Mercedes has yet to publicly oppose or endorse. Read more

articles.title: El gran desafío de Eva Moral: dos Mundiales en 15 días
articles.standfirst: La medallista paralímpica afronta, a partir de este viernes, el Campeonato del mundo de ciclismo y después el de triatlón. Aspira a clasificarse en ambos deportes para los Juegos de Los Ángeles 2028
articles.summary: La
articles.body: Su lema es Never give up (Nunca te rindas). Lo lleva tatuado en la muñeca derecha. En la izquierda luce una silla de atletismo, “la carroza de la muerte” como la propia Eva Moral la bautizó la primera vez que se subió a una tras el accidente. El 29 de este mes hará 13 años que, durante una carrera cicloturista por la sierra de Madrid, se cayó por un barranco de siete metros y se produjo una lesión medular. Entonces trabajaba como abogada en una entidad financiera y el deporte era su gran hobby. “Era mi vía de escape. Hacía triatlón y competía a nivel nacional. Tras el accidente tuve claro que necesitaba el deporte en mi vida y una de las cosas que me más me preocupaban al principio era que se hubiese acabado porque me daba la vida”, confiesa. Lo hace tras entrenar con la silla de atletismo en el Patinódromo de Parla, donde nos ha citado a las 10:00 horas. Antes, a las 8:00, ya estaba nadando en la piscina. También entrena con su handbike el ciclismo y el físico en el gimnasio. En total le dedica entre 7 y 8 horas al día. Moral está un poco acatarrada pero es de las que no perdona un entrenamiento. De hecho, entrena los siete días de la semana. “Bueno, hay uno que se supone que es más flojo pero todavía no me he enterado mucho de cuál es. Preguntádselo a Ángel”, dice riendo. Se refiere a Ángel Salamanca, su entrenador, marido y handler (asistente que ayuda al deportista durante la competición, sobre todo en las transiciones y en la salida del agua). Juntos han formado, además de una bonita familia con su hija Carmen, un tándem ganador. Al principio eran José y Rosario, sus padres, quienes la acompañaban por el mundo a las competiciones. “Los comienzos son muy duros y muy caros porque tienes que viajar por todo el mundo cuando no tienes resultado, ni ranking ni ayudas. Yo aposté todo lo que tenía, todo, para luchar por el sueño de estar en unos Juegos Paralímpicos. Ya cuando estaba en el Hospital Nacional de Parapléjicos de Toledo me hablaron de que el triatlón iba a ser paralímpico en Rio 2016 (aunque su categoría no fue incluida). Todo el dinero que tenía me lo gasté en viajar por el mundo compitiendo con mis padres”, explica. No sólo era caro viajar, también lo era –y sigue siéndolo– el material con el que compite. “La dificultad que tiene el deporte paralímpico, y en concreto el triatlón para las personas que vamos en silla de ruedas, es precisamente el coste del material, que además es muy específico. Tú no vas a una tienda y pides una silla de atletismo o una handbike (bicicleta impulsada con las manos en lugar de las piernas). Son a medida y las ruedas también son caras. Y desde que se está profesionalizando el deporte paralímpico hay más avances tecnológicos y no te puedes quedar atrás. Hay años luz de la primera handbike que yo tuve a la de ahora. Al final lo que menos cuesta es nadar porque te compras un bañador y listo”, explica. Una handbike con ruedas buenas puede estar en torno a 20.000 € y la silla de atletismo entre 15.000 y 16.000. En 2014, cuando comenzó a competir, poco podía imaginar que se convertiría en una de las triatletas más exitosas de nuestro país como corrobora un palmarés en el que hay un bronce paralímpico (Tokio 2020), siete oros europeos y varias medallas mundiales. El oro europeo de 2021 y el bronce mundial de ese mismo año en Abu Dabi los ganó estando embarazada. “La conciliación de la maternidad con el deporte de élite son los abuelos. Ya está”, asegura con rotundidad. “Me quedé embarazada nada más llegar de Tokio y a los dos meses y medio de dar a luz ya estaba compitiendo porque si no, no me daba el ranking. Tuve que volver a hacer todas las competiciones del calendario con un bebé lactante que tuvo que viajar por todo el mundo conmigo sin ningún tipo de ayuda. Pagaba los viajes a mis padres para que me acompañasen y ellos cuidaran de Carmen mientras yo entrenaba y competía”, explica sobre la realidad de compaginar deporte de élite y maternidad. “Físicamente es complicado recuperarse y volver a tu estado de forma, pero es más difícil psicológicamente”, añade. A ella le pasó factura en el ciclo hacia los Juegos de París. “No sé ni cómo llegué de cabeza. Es difícil, pero Carmen es lo mejor que me ha pasado en la vida, es mi mejor medalla y mi mayor motivación”, reconoce. Por eso, cada día entrena de 08:00 a 17:00, pero a partir de esa hora se centra en su hija o, como dice ella, en “maternar”. Al echar la vista atrás, la medallista paralímpica hace un balance muy positivo. Reconoce que cuando ingresó en el Hospital 12 de octubre tras el accidente o cuando estaba reconstruyendo su vida en el Hospital Nacional de Parapléjicos de Toledo no podía ni imaginar todo lo que iba a vivir. “No voy a romantizar la discapacidad, ni mucho menos. Lo que me pasó fue una cosa horrible en nuestras vidas, no sólo para mí sino para todos los que me rodeaban. Fue un palo muy gordo. Y sobreponerse de eso te hace mucho más fuerte. Pero muchas veces digo todo que lo mejor que tengo en mi vida ha ocurrido en estos 13 años: conocer a mi marido, tener a mi hija, ganar un bronce paralímpico que me supo a oro, ir a dos Juegos... No puedo pedir más. De verdad que son cosas que ni podía soñar entonces”, confiesa con una amplia sonrisa. El primer reportaje que le hicimos en MARCA fue en enero de 2014. Se llevó la bronca de uno de los médicos del Hospital de Parapléjicos porque estuvo más tiempo de la cuenta en la handbike. “Cuando la probé por primera vez tuve una sensación muy buena, de libertad, de sentir otra vez el viento en la cara y tuve claro que quería hacer eso. Me hablaron del triatlón paralímpico, que ni siquiera conocía que existía, y fue una motivación”, explica. El ciclismo, al ser uno de los tres segmentos del triatlón, ha estado presente en su día a día estos 13 años. Durante este tiempo ha acudido a varios campeonatos de España como mero entrenamiento porque le venía bien para el triatlón. Desde el año pasado, Moral compagina campeonatos de ambos deportes. En 2025 ya acudió a varias Copas del Mundo y al Mundial de carretera, sin dejar a un lado el triatlón. “Para Los Ángeles 2028, el Team Relay (relevo por equipos) va a ser mixto. La seleccionadora (Begoña Luis) está haciendo un buen trabajo para que haya más mujeres dentro de la selección en un deporte que mayoritariamente ha sido masculino. Está apostando fuerte por nosotras”, dice. En el Mundial de carretera de Huntsville (Alabama, Estados Unidos), del 4 al 7 de septiembre, participará en todas las pruebas. “Mi objetivo es seguir aprendiendo. Obviamente no tenemos ninguna pretensión más allá de hacerlo bien y que nos salgan los tiempos que tenemos planteados”, reconoce. Poco más de 15 días después –el día 25– disputará su segundo Mundial, esta vez en triatlón. Todo un desafío que vayan tan seguidos. “Prefiero no pensarlo”, dice entre risas. “Al final el que tiene que hacer más cábalas es Ángel, que tiene que hacer la planificación para intentar que llegue en la mejor posición posible en ambos deportes. Estos años estoy haciendo bastante más bici y hemos visto que los resultados siguen saliendo. Es una apuesta”, dice. De cara al Mundial de Pontevedra es mucho más ambiciosa. “Estar lo más arriba posible. Y ahí nos jugamos la beca del año que viene. Pero el objetivo principal es intentar clasificarme para Los Ángeles en ambos deportes. Sería la primera vez que una mujer española en silla de ruedas consigue este hito”, asegura. “Creo que el triatlón es al principio de los Juegos y el ciclismo al final. Así que me quedaría en Los Ángeles una temporada”, dice entre risas.
